title: Controls on the deformation and reorientation of mafic enclaves during magma mingling: A computational study
abstract: Mafic microgranular enclaves in granitic plutons record magma mingling, and their shapes are often interpreted as a record of the flow that deformed them. We investigate how a dense, low-viscosity droplet deforms in a lighter, much more viscous host under shear and gravity, using 96 two-dimensional Level-Set simulations. The viscosity ratio ($\mu_r$) spans $10^{-6}$ - $10^{-3}$, the capillary number ($\mathrm{Ca}$) ranges from $10^{6}$ to $8\times10^{9}$, the Bond number ($\mathrm{Bo}$) takes values of $3.5\times10^{6}$ and $9.8\times10^{6}$, and the Reynolds number ($\mathrm{Re}$) remains below $10^{-2}$, with a fixed density contrast ($\Delta\rho$) of $400~\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. Two broad regimes identified- sinking and non-sinking which spread over six outcomes like sinking, edge, mid and multiple break-up, rotation, and retraction. The ratio $\mathrm{Ca/Bo}$ separates sinking from shear-dominated behaviour near unity, although the transition spans a range of $\mathrm{Ca/Bo}$ values that shifts with confinement. In the shear-dominated regime, a lower viscosity ratio promotes stretching. Multiple pinch-off occurs mainly at viscosity ratios of $10^{-6}$ - $10^{-5}$, rotation occurs only at the higher vertical confinement, and retraction occurs only at the lower vertical confinement. The strain at maximum stretch averages 1.1 - 1.4 and increases with $\mathrm{Ca/Bo}$, with a stronger increase at higher confinement. The orientation of the major axis decreases by approximately $10^\circ$ per unit strain and is lowest for rotating droplets. Because the capillary number exceeds conventional critical values for breakup for droplets, breakup is interpreted in terms of accumulated deformation rather than capillary stability alone. Enclave shape therefore reflects the flow regime and is not a direct measure of finite strain.

title: Discovering like a scientist: Literature-informed dimensionless learning for physical closure of data-driven equations
abstract: Data-driven methods can recover compact equations, yet the physical dependence of their coefficients across operating conditions often remains unresolved. Dimensionless groups can explain this variation, but selecting relevant groups from the many dimensionally admissible combinations remains challenging. Here, we introduce a knowledge-guided framework for dimensionless learning, called {\pi}-former. It learns patterns of variable association and exponent assignment from a corpus of 1,288 established dimensionless groups. Under exact dimensional constraints, the model proposes interpretable basic groups whose combinations are optimized against observations. Across seven physical problems, the framework identifies predictive dimensionless coordinates within seconds. Integration with equation discovery further expresses condition-dependent coefficients through these coordinates, recovering established physical scalings in multi-condition simulations. Applied to experimental measurements of evaporation-driven wetting, the framework discovers dimensionless coordinates and uses them to construct a unified trajectory equation. The resulting model generalizes to held-out conditions across liquids and initial volumes, outperforming existing empirical models. These results establish dimensionless learning as a transferable bridge between accumulated scientific knowledge and data-driven equation discovery, enabling artificial intelligence to uncover physically meaningful laws from observations.

title: A coupled lattice Boltzmann model for pore-scale mushy-layer dynamics with application to sea ice
abstract: A pore-scale lattice Boltzmann model is developed for reactive transport in phase-changing porous media, coupling solute transport in the liquid with conjugate heat transfer across the solid and liquid phases. Two methodological developments are introduced: a novel link-based Volume-of-Pixel formulation for direction-dependent interface motion, and a generalized Robin boundary treatment for solute redistribution at moving interfaces. The phase-change formulation is validated against thermal benchmarks, while the Robin treatment is assessed through literature test cases, exhibiting convergence rates between first and second order. The coupled model is then applied to a local pore-scale segment of a sea ice brine channel in a purely diffusive regime. The simulations recover the expected ideal mushy-layer behaviour under appropriate scale separation. At sea-ice-relevant concentration ratios, thermal perturbations produce relatively large variations in brine salinity, causing freezing rather than melting to reshape the pore geometry in a non-uniform way. The resulting framework provides a pore-scale numerical tool for resolving coupled temperature, solute redistribution, and phase-boundary dynamics in mushy layers.

title: Energy-Guided Transport for Projection-Free Physics-Informed Flow Matching
abstract: Deep generative models, particularly Flow Matching frameworks, have emerged as powerful tools for synthesizing complex physical systems. However, standard architectures remain purely statistically driven and agnostic to the underlying governing equations, often violating fundamental physical constraints during inference. Existing zero-shot approaches designed to enforce these constraints typically rely on rigid algebraic projections. While effective for sparse boundary conditions, applying such discrete geometric corrections to dense, full-domain PDEs may disrupt the probability path, \rev{potentially deviating from the learned manifold and introducing substantial computational overhead}. To address these challenges, we introduce Energy-Guided Transport, a novel training-free framework that formulates non-linear physical constraints as a smooth potential energy landscape. Rather than interrupting the ODE integration, our method applies a continuous dissipative force directly to the intermediate generative states, steering them toward the physical manifold. By evaluating this force implicitly via reverse-mode automatic differentiation, our framework preserves the natural dynamics of the flow while maintaining an efficient $\mathcal{O}(N)$ algorithmic complexity. We extensively evaluate our framework across various 1D and 2D physical systems, including the chaotic Navier-Stokes equations. Our method achieves stable generation without structural divergence, significantly improves the stability-accuracy trade-off compared to state-of-the-art methods, and substantially accelerates inference with respect to exact projection strategies. Code available at: https://github.com/ispamm/Projection-free-energy-guided-flow-matching.

title: Quantum Spin Wave Theory with Multi-Spin Interactions for Magnetic Materials Modeling
abstract: In the field of magnetism within condensed matter physics, magnetic systems are microscopically described by a spin Hamiltonian. Its parameterization is accessible through both ab initio calculations and fits to experimental data. Frequently, this is achieved via multi-stage calculations that either relate the parameters to observable material properties or map a Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian onto an effective spin model. In this realm, accurate and flexible methods are essential for simulating the physical properties of the latter. The present study focuses on one such method: spin wave theory. The approach is applied to a new formulation of the spin Hamiltonian, named polynomial localized spin model (PLSM), which includes terms of arbitrary order in the spin operators. This enables the direct application of linear spin wave theory (LSWT) to the analysis of the energy landscape and spin-wave spectrum of arbitrary collinear and non-collinear phases in any realistic magnetic material. Moreover, the classical and quantum parts of the PLSM are cleanly separated. Finally, an open-source implementation of LSWT, named Magnopy, is presented. It interfaces with modern parameterization software, supports arbitrary collinear and non-collinear systems, and is designed for both scripting and standalone use.
